provider.notes: Registered under the single id 'assemblyai' (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1691; gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:406-408); no aliases. default_model records what happens today for an English or empty language: the gateway picks universal-streaming-english; for any other language it picks universal-streaming-multilingual (gateway/src/core/stt/assemblyai/config.rs:450-456). The field can hold only one id, so the resolver must apply the same language rule before the lookup, also when placeholder_as_unset turns the placeholder 'nova-3' into no model named: the client on its own serves the English model for 'nova-3' whatever the language (config.rs:118-125, 456-459), so the resolver must hand the resolved id to the client. AssemblyAI has three interfaces on three hosts: the streaming socket (streaming.assemblyai.com), the synchronous Sync API (sync.assemblyai.com, which serves universal-3-5-pro only) and the asynchronous job API (api.assemblyai.com). The gateway has one endpoint override shared by all of them and knows only the default and Europe streaming hosts (config.rs:137-153). The streaming client replaces every model id it does not know, including universal-3-6-pro, universal-3-5-pro and universal-2, with universal-streaming-english (config.rs:118-125). The rows for those ids therefore list no streaming transport, and when_unusable records the substitution: such a session keeps today's stream with the warning stt_model_substituted, universal-3-5-pro moves to the Sync API in Release 3, default on, and universal-2 is refused from that release. Fixing the client (send the id, refuse unknown ids) would let those rows list the streaming socket again. The client has a method that sends a forced end-of-turn message (gateway/src/core/stt/assemblyai/client.rs:1084-1106) with no caller; no gateway-driven commit transport is listed because the vendor's current support for that message is not in the fetched evidence. The client's own short name 'multilingual' is a model alias on the universal-streaming-multilingual row.

gateway_client.notes: Nothing under gateway/src names the Sync host or its path; the file-upload code for this vendor speaks only the asynchronous job API. The Sync request is POST /v1/transcribe on sync.assemblyai.com (also sync.us and sync.eu): multipart, an audio part and a JSON config part, with the model named in the required header X-AAI-Model. One request returns one JSON body; there is no job and no polling. The vendor documents it for exactly this use: one utterance cut by a voice detector per request, padded with half a second of trailing silence. In the config part the language field is language_codes (one code or a list, default en, no automatic detection, ignored when prompt is set); prior turns go in conversation_context and vocabulary in keyterms_prompt. A no-operation request, GET /v1/warm, exists to open the connection when speech starts. Rate-limit and capacity responses carry Retry-After; a server error or server timeout is safe to retry once.

segment_profile.rationale: Maximum segment 60 s instead of 25 s: the 25 s default protects Whisper's 30 s window, which does not apply here. The Sync API accepts up to 120 s and the vendor says audio under about a minute is handled as one internal segment. 60 s is a judgement from the vendor audit, not a vendor number; the hard ceiling is 120 s including pre-roll and padding, and the floor is 80 ms. Request timeout 4 s with one retry: about six times the published 0.65 s 99th percentile and far below the vendor's 30 s server deadline; replace it with a deadline from measurement.

transports.disabled_reason: Not implemented for live sessions, and this is an asynchronous job API: upload the audio, submit a job, then poll for the result. AssemblyAI publishes no latency for short clips, only that most files finish in under 45 seconds. Keep it disabled unless a measurement shows a final transcript within about two seconds.

gateway_client.notes: The pieces exist for the file-upload routes only, and neither is reachable from a live session. There is a builder for the job submission, which is always asynchronous (batch.rs:512-518, 640-644), and there are two separate drivers. The upload-route driver uploads, submits and polls; it sends once, when the session disconnects (prerecorded.rs:1098-1112); its first poll is at 500 ms, polls back off to 3 s and its deadline and HTTP timeout are both 300 s (prerecorded.rs:72-94). The batch route has its own upload and submit code (gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:600-631, 636-663). A per-utterance adapter has two drivers to reconcile, not one. A live turn would need its own short deadline and a faster first poll, and polls count against the vendor's request limit.

provenance.notes: The same id is valid on three AssemblyAI interfaces: the streaming socket, the synchronous Sync API and the asynchronous job API. The transport must therefore be chosen by the kind of session, never by the id alone. The vendor describes this model as its previous flagship streaming model, still fully supported. None of the three is usable from the gateway today: the streaming client substitutes another model, and neither file adapter is built. The Sync API is the transport the segmented design should build first for this vendor: it is one request per utterance with a published 99th percentile of 0.65 s, about 0.2 s slower than the same vendor's socket. The Sync transport is enabled from Release 3, default on (integration decisions, sections 6 and 12); until then a session naming this model keeps today's substituted stream with the warning stt_model_substituted (when_unusable). The streaming socket is not listed, because today's client cannot select this model.

measurements.conditions: Pipecat's shipped constant ASSEMBLYAI_TTFS_P99 = 0.42 s (time from end of speech to final transcript, voice detector hangover 0.2 s). The evidence does not say which AssemblyAI streaming model Pipecat measured, so this is a provider-level seed, not a measurement of this model. Not measured by WaaV on this network. AssemblyAI's own benchmark page gives a different measure, time to complete a turn: a median of 649 ms and a 90th percentile of 990 ms on Universal Streaming English, and 568 ms and 829 ms on Universal-3.5 Pro streaming (May 2026). On a live call the gateway waits for AssemblyAI to end the turn, so the vendor's figures may describe today's path better than Pipecat's (inferred); if they do, this transport belongs in the 'fast' class, not 'realtime'. Measure before showing this class to customers.

gateway_client.defect: With formatted turns requested by default, AssemblyAI sends two end-of-turn messages per turn and the message type cannot tell them apart, so a turn can be delivered twice; the detected language is read from a field named language although the vendor sends language_code; a full result channel drops a final. Found by reading, not reproduced on a live call.
gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against in-repo mock sockets (a mock end-to-end test and a reconnect test); the evidence records no run against AssemblyAI. Each caller chunk is written at once as one binary frame (client.rs:180-191). Every vendor Turn message becomes a result whose is_final and is_speech_final both equal the vendor's end_of_turn flag (client.rs:520-525), so AssemblyAI alone decides where the caller's turn ends. Defects found by reading, not reproduced on a live call: the client asks for formatted turns by default (config.rs:283), for which AssemblyAI documents two end-of-turn messages per turn, and the message type has no field to tell them apart (messages.rs:56-76), so each turn can be delivered twice; the detected language is read from a field named language while the vendor sends language_code (messages.rs:70-72); a full result channel drops a final and logs it as a closed channel (client.rs:527-529).

gateway_client.notes: Nothing under gateway/src names the Sync host or its path; the file-upload code for this vendor speaks only the asynchronous job API. The Sync request is POST /v1/transcribe on sync.assemblyai.com (also sync.us and sync.eu): multipart, an audio part and a JSON config part, with the model named in the required header X-AAI-Model. One request returns one JSON body; there is no job and no polling. The vendor documents it for exactly this use: one utterance cut by a voice detector per request, padded with half a second of trailing silence. In the config part the language field is language_codes (one code or a list, default en, no automatic detection, ignored when prompt is set); prior turns go in conversation_context and vocabulary in keyterms_prompt. A no-operation request, GET /v1/warm, exists to open the connection when speech starts. Rate-limit and capacity responses carry Retry-After; a server error or server timeout is safe to retry once.

segment_profile.rationale: Maximum segment 60 s instead of 25 s: the 25 s default protects Whisper's 30 s window, which does not apply here. The Sync API accepts up to 120 s and the vendor says audio under about a minute is handled as one internal segment. 60 s is a judgement from the vendor audit, not a vendor number; the hard ceiling is 120 s including pre-roll and padding, and the floor is 80 ms. Request timeout 4 s with one retry: about six times the published 0.65 s 99th percentile and far below the vendor's 30 s server deadline; replace it with a deadline from measurement.
